newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN IPO - Victory Glass & Industries Ltd.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN IPO - Victory Glass & Industries Ltd.

text.p: The following initial public issue (IPO) by India's Victory Glass & Industries Ltd is expected to be open for public subscription on September 26:
(*) Fully Convertible Debentures of 85 rupees each.

Public issue of fully convertible debentures from Victory Glass is to finance expansion of glass bottle manufacturing, to set up a windpower project and a pet bottle manufacturing unit. The total cost estimated at 272 million rupees is proposed to be financed through 64 million rupees rights issue, 105 million rupees public issue, 80 million rupees term loans and 22.53 million rupees internal accruals.

Each FCD of 85 rupees will have two parts, Part A of 40 rupees and Part B of 45 rupees. Part A will be converted into one share of 10 rupees at the time of allotment at a premium of 30 rupees. Part B will be converted into one share of 10 rupees at a premium of 35 rupees on 1 April 1997.

The company has already spent 118 million rupees for the project drawing funds from term loans, internal accruals and advance against rights issue from the promoters. The glass manufacturing capacity has been expanded from 31,000 tpa (tonnes per annum) to 36,500 tpa at the existing plant in Bangalore district.

The annual power requirements of the plant is estimated at 5.40 million units to be bought from the state electricity board. To reduce power costs the company has installed nine wind energy generators of 225 KW each at a cost of 105 million rupees. The power generated is expected to meet the plant's entire need. The wind energy generators are located at Nagavi village, Dharwad district in Karnataka.

The proposed PET bottle project to be located at Ponda in Goa will have an installed capacity of 22 million bottles per annum. The estimated project cost is 100 million rupees and is expected to start commercial production in March 1997. The company would sell PET bottles directly to the end users without involving dealers or distributors.
For the year ended March 1996, the company on a turnover of 269 million rupees made a net profit of 32 million rupees. EPS on a equity capital of 22.90 rupees worked out to 14.10 rupees.
